A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoccerMaster research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched across renaming and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation-pipeline evaluations, SoccerMaster benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative predictions in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and reports revised pretraining-task scores and full-model ablation results.

M1.justification: The encoder, task heads, losses, annotation pipeline, and downstream adaptations remain unchanged. Renaming athlete detection to detection and identification describes role and jersey-number outputs already present in v1; newly specified component variants are implementation disclosures.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same soccer datasets, tasks, and camera-view scenarios. Tables 2 and 8 preserve dataset composition and sample counts. The SoccerFactory renaming and expanded discussion of other datasets do not establish new experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1 and 3–6, including the GSR challenge pipelines, SigLIP 2, DINOv3, MatchVision, PnlCalib, and YOLOv8-based trackers. Newly cited works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Previously stated splits, resolutions, training budgets, metrics, and frozen-encoder comparison procedures remain unchanged. Additional pipeline settings are newly disclosed details. The calibration-metrics appendix repeats definitions already given in v1 Section 6.2.

E4.justification: The full-scale single-task versus multi-task ablation has revised evidence in v2 Appendix D: single-task detection changes from slight advantages to slight disadvantages. Its question and design remain the same. The compact-model ablation, generated-data ablation, and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Revised point estimates do not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises SoccerMaster's scores under the same reported protocol: detection mAP changes from 50.5 to 49.5, event accuracy from 73.8 to 77.2, and retrieval top-1 from 35.0 to 39.0. Line recall changes from 93.0 to 92.4, falling below DINOv3's unchanged 92.7. Full-scale single-task AP@50/mAP advantages of +0.5/+0.5 become −0.3/−0.5. Other result tables and qualitative examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Task definitions and Equations 1–14 retain their mathematical content. The new calibration-metrics appendix restates existing definitions rather than introducing mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a unified soccer model, automated annotation supporting combined pretraining data, and strong downstream performance. Terminology revisions do not expand the claimed capabilities.

C2.justification: The revised ablation still supports the same capacity-based explanation for multi-task interference and comparable full-model performance. Interpretations of transferability and limitations concerning jersey recognition, goalkeeper classification, and absent ball tracking remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix A.2.1 specifies selecting main-camera-center shots using SoccerNet annotations and partitioning clips at 30 seconds. New Appendix B.2 identifies detector checkpoints, tracking-weight provenance, YOLOv8x6 fine-tuning data, and Qwen2.5-VL 7B/72B assignments for role/jersey recognition. These improve documentation without establishing procedural changes.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a Soccer Datasets discussion positioning the pipeline against fragmented annotations and scarce dense main-camera labels. Six references are added, including SoccerNet-depth, VersaViT, MRGen, and OmniStream; the earlier cited works are retained.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites redefine SoccerFactory as the pipeline rather than the combined dataset and expand athlete-detection terminology. The appendix gains separate implementation subsections and a repeated calibration-metrics explanation. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains explicit subpanel labels and revised task headings; several table headers, captions, sizes, and placements change. All six figures and twelve tables remain, with unchanged qualitative imagery. The expanded contents list spills onto a largely blank additional page.

improvement.justification: The added clip-selection instructions and pipeline component specifications address concrete documentation gaps in v1, modestly improving reproducibility. Expanded dataset positioning also helps explain the contribution. These gains are limited by naming inconsistencies: Table 1 attributes pipeline results to SoccerMaster, while Appendix A.4 still calls the dataset SoccerFactory. Revised scores alone do not establish better paper quality.
